fanTake: The Patriots absolutely suffocated Pittsburgh on Sunday, limiting the Steelers to a field goal in a 20-3 domination at Gillette—and this defensive performance might just be the signature win of the season so far. Our defense posted a -0.36 EPA per play allowed, the third-best mark by any team in 2026, and held Pittsburgh scoreless in the end zone while forcing them to convert just 17% of their third downs; that's the kind of suffocating football that wins you division games. Offensively we weren't lighting it up—negative EPA per play, below-average third-down conversion, and we punched in a touchdown on only one of three red-zone trips—but honestly, when your defense is playing like that, you don't need much. Romeo Doubs was our catalyst through the air, adding 14% win probability on his own, and the whole operation was simply the kind of controlled, professional win you dream about. This is the first time we've beaten Pittsburgh since 2023, and with only 3 points allowed—our best defensive output since Week 10 of last season—this one's going to feel good for a while.
